summary: This article explains how Earth's two cold polar regions compare: the Arctic is a frozen ocean ringed by land, the Antarctic is an icy continent that is also a desert, and each has its own animals and people.
introduce: Draw two overlapping circles on the board and quickly compare two familiar things, such as a cat and a dog, with the class. Tell students that while reading “The Arctic and the Antarctic” they will look for ways things are alike and different.

keyTerms.def: having to do with the cold areas near the North or South Pole
the amount that a line or ray is tilted
a very thick layer of ice that covers a large area of land

challengeTerms.def: one half of the Earth, such as the northern or southern half
water that falls from the sky as rain, snow, sleet, or hail
belonging to the first people or living things of a place

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that I would rather visit the Antarctic than the Arctic? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why the Antarctic is called a desert even though it is covered in ice.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review polar, angle, and ice sheet, and let weak readers fill in a T-chart of alike and different with sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses hemisphere, precipitation, and indigenous to compare two ideas from the article and explain which difference matters most.
